**The register is a declaration, not a behaviour claim.** The command surface is built from `surface/dispatch-table.json`, so the register at a revision states what that revision exposes. It does not state that any of it works. Where this page and your binary disagree, **your binary is right**.

**Exit codes are stated for 5 of these 6 commands, and that is the register's coverage rather than an omission here.** A row carries the exit codes measured on _v2_; whether v3 reproduces them is a separate field. Where the register says v3 corrects v2 without recording what it corrects it to, this page says so instead of reprinting the behaviour the rewrite exists to remove.

## The commands

| Command               | What it does                                        | In v3.0.0 | Reads or writes | Undo       |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | --------- | --------------- | ---------- |
| `intent issues`       | Track issues without the ceremony of a steel thread | yes       | read            | --         |
| `intent issues list`  | List issues (default: open)                         | yes       | read            | --         |
| `intent issues add`   | Add a new issue, print its ID:TITLE                 | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent issues show`  | Show one issue (optionally as JSON)                 | yes       | read            | --         |
| `intent issues close` | Mark an issue done: OPEN -> CLOSED                  | yes       | mutate          | reversible |
| `intent issues open`  | Reopen an issue: CLOSED -> OPEN                     | yes       | mutate          | reversible |

## Retired

These do not exist in v3. They refuse with an exit code that distinguishes _removed_ from _never built_, so a v2-era script gets an answer rather than an unknown-command error.

| Command                   | What it did in v2                                      |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `intent issues hydrate`   | Add an issue to .intentfiles and write its files       |
| `intent issues dehydrate` | Remove an issue from .intentfiles and delete its files |

## `intent issues`

Track issues without the ceremony of a steel thread

```
intent issues [<command>] [flags]
```

|                 |                                                            |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| In `v3.0.0`     | yes                                                        |
| Reads or writes | read                                                       |
| Undo            | not applicable -- the register records this verb as a read |
| Over MCP        | no                                                         |

**Arguments**

| Argument  | Type         | Required | Values | Notes |
| --------- | ------------ | -------- | ------ | ----- |
| `command` | `subcommand` | no       |        | list  |

**Flags**

| Flag       | Takes              | Default    | What it does                                                     |
| ---------- | ------------------ | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--width`  | `<n>`              |            | Render at a fixed column width; 0 or absent means terminal width |
| `--format` | `terminal` or `md` | `terminal` | Output format                                                    |

**Exit codes.** v3 reproduces the behaviour measured on v2 for this verb.

| Code | When                                                                                       |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 0    | bare -- defaults to `list`, prints `no open issues` and exits 0                            |
| 0    | `--help` -- 577B usage to STDOUT, exit 0                                                   |
| 1    | unknown verb -- `error: Unknown issues command '<v>'. Run 'intent issues help' for usage.` |
| 1    | outside a project -- `error: not in an Intent project directory` (INV-03)                  |

## `intent issues add`

Add a new issue, print its ID:TITLE

```
intent issues add <title> [flags]
```

Also spelled `issues new`.

|                 |            |
| --------------- | ---------- |
| In `v3.0.0`     | yes        |
| Reads or writes | mutate     |
| Undo            | reversible |
| Over MCP        | yes        |

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type     | Required | Values | Notes |
| -------- | -------- | -------- | ------ | ----- |
| `title`  | `string` | yes      |        |       |

**Flags**

| Flag         | Takes                                     | Default  | What it does                       |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------- |
| `--severity` | `critical` or `high` or `medium` or `low` | `medium` | Severity                           |
| `--body`     | `<text>`                                  |          | The issue's prose, inline          |
| `--from`     | `<file>`                                  |          | Read the issue's prose from a file |

**The register records that v3 corrects v2 on this verb and does not record what it corrects it TO.** The measured exit codes it carries are v2's, and v2's are what the correction exists to change, so they are not reproduced here. `intent issues add --help`, and your own binary, are the authority.

| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| In `v3.0.0`     | yes                                                        |
| Reads or writes | read                                                       |

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type       | Required | Values | Notes |
| -------- | ---------- | -------- | ------ | ----- |
| `id`     | `issue-id` | yes      |        |       |

**Flags**

| Flag       | Takes                        | Default    | What it does                  |
| ---------- | ---------------------------- | ---------- | ----------------------------- |
| `--json`   | no                           |            | Emit as JSON instead of prose |
| `--format` | `terminal` or `md` or `json` | `terminal` | Output format                 |

| Code | When                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | printed                                                                                                                                                                       |

| 1    | outside a project -- `error: not in an Intent project directory` (INV-03)                                                                                                     |

## `intent issues close`

Mark an issue done: OPEN -> CLOSED

```
intent issues close <id>
```

|                 |            |
| --------------- | ---------- |
| In `v3.0.0`     | yes        |
| Reads or writes | mutate     |
| Undo            | reversible |
| Over MCP        | yes        |

**Arguments**

| Argument | Type       | Required | Values | Notes |
| -------- | ---------- | -------- | ------ | ----- |
| `id`     | `issue-id` | yes      |        |       |

**Exit codes.** v3 reproduces the behaviour measured on v2 for this verb.

| Code | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | closed -- `ok: issue <ID> -> CLOSED` (bin/intent_issues:291)                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| 0    | ALREADY in the target bucket -- `ok: issue <ID> already CLOSED`, exit 0 (bin/intent_issues:280-283). **This is v2's ONLY `already` arm and the one hv's self-loop ruling cites**; `move_issue` checks the SOURCE bucket, and on a miss checks the TARGET before erroring. |
| 1    | in NEITHER bucket -- `error: Issue not found in OPEN: <ID>` (bin/intent_issues:285). The message names the BUCKET, not just the id.                                                                                                                                       |
| 1    | outside a project -- `error: not in an Intent project directory` (INV-03)                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## Refusals

**There is no per-command refusal list, because the register does not carry one.** A row declares its path, arguments, flags, target, disposition, recoverability, MCP exposure and read-or-mutate, and nothing structural about what it refuses. Where a command's exit codes appear above, those _are_ its refusal contract; where they do not, the register has nothing to publish.

The estate-wide roster of refusal variants is in [what Intent ships at this revision](cut-surface.md), taken from a roster that declares itself exhaustive and is checked as one. **It is not attributed to commands anywhere**, and attributing it by reading the variant names would be a guess dressed as a reference.
